chunks: Ali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Yamani, who said:

I was in Baghdad, and a caravan for the Yemenis had been prepared, and I wanted to go out with it. So I wrote seeking permission concerning that, and there came out: “Do not go out with them, for there is no good choice for you in going out with them, and remain in al-Kufah.”

He said: I stayed, and the caravan departed. Then Hanzalah came out against them and overwhelmed them. And I wrote seeking permission to travel by water, but he did not permit me. So I asked about the ships that had gone out upon the sea in that year, and not a single ship among them was saved. A people from India, called al-Bawarij, came out against them and cut them off.

He said: I visited al-'Askar, then I came to the passageway at sunset, and I did not speak to anyone nor make myself known to anyone. While I was performing salat (prayer) in the masjid after finishing the ziyarah, suddenly a servant had come to me and said to me, “Rise.” So I said to him, “Then where to?” He said to me, “To the house.” I said, “And who am I? Perhaps you were sent to someone other than me.” He said, “No, I was sent only to you. You are Ali ibn al-Husayn, the messenger of Ja'far ibn Ibrahim.”

So he took me along until he lodged me in the house of al-Husayn ibn Ahmad. Then he spoke privately with him, and I did not know what he said to him, until he brought me everything that I needed. And I stayed with him for three days, and I sought his permission for the ziyarah from inside, so he permitted me, and I visited at night.

key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: the visitation he completed and later sought permission to perform from inside
key_terms.الْإِذْنَ: permission sought from the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْبَوَارِجُ: a group identified as attackers from India
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: the city where he was instructed to remain
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the masjid where he was performing salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imam’s guidance and protection in travel decisions?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts how Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Yamani sought permission before traveling and was instructed to remain, after which the caravan and the sea journeys he had considered were struck by disaster. It also narrates his visit to al-'Askar and how he was recognized and hosted through hidden guidance, reflecting the care and direction associated with the Imam عليه السلام.
